question: Connect observed burden, preference, actual switching and expert expectations to PHVS acquisition assumptions; do not presume a short conclusion.
verdict: Evidence supports burden-sensitive switching, but neither dissatisfaction-only TAM nor a uniform second-oral acquisition discount. No empirically identified PHVS capture or taper rate.

sources.population: 328 commercially insured US non-androgen LTP initiators, 2016-Sep2023;39 berotralstat
sources.interpretation: Higher prior rescue use among later switchers supports residual-burden targeting. Association does not estimate P(switch|poor control). Switch includes return to original drug. Different initiator population; not Orladeyo-specific. Source sponsored by KalVista.

sources.population: 150 US survey respondents in October2023;139 on LTP;only9 berotralstat in treatment-specific table
sources.interpretation: Control and burden affect interest; route preference exists independently. Not national paid switching. Do not multiply by claims switch rate or general access conversion as if one cohort.

sources.population: 65 enrolled switch volunteers;64 treated;11 prior berotralstat;Ionis funded
sources.interpretation: An oral incumbent can be displaced by injection. Controlled patients also chose to switch. Neither 22/64 poor control nor11/11 continuing identifies national dissatisfaction or capture. Open label, selected switchers, reasons not collected, no comparator; not proof of PHVS outcome.

sources.population: Jan2023-Jan2024 multinational physician survey1131 records;279 adult patient questionnaires;pre-Ekterly
sources.interpretation: High satisfaction coexists at sample level with strong oral-rescue interest; no joint cross-tab proves individual overlap. Not US Orladeyo-specific and not post-Ekterly oral-to-oral interest. Pharvaris supported analysis/interpretation/publication; original Adelphi survey independent of Pharvaris design/data collection. No automatic market shares.

sources.finding: Small practice would not proactively move well-controlled users; administrative friction. Supports lower stable-user hazard, not zero nationwide switching.

20-25%, up to25-30% possible overall switching;33-40% new-start preference; no defined horizon or paid endpoint. Clinical factual inaccuracies elsewhere and speculative dual coverage mean use as opinion only; do not average with other potentially repeat Optum calls.
Perceived efficacy benefit but only two current Orladeyo users, uncertain whether they would switch. Does not quantify capture.

sources.interpretation: Company forms, not paid starts. About20% slowdown then stable across last two intervals. Annual27.4% is PHVS model calibration, not reported Ekterly hazard. No multi-year taper identified.

architecture_recommendation.XR: Within each current-treatment pool, separate meaningful efficacy/control burden from remaining patients with possible convenience preference. Treat these as mutually exclusive states; former oral users remain in current-treatment stock. p_rx(t)=d(t)*p_rx_burden(t)+(1-d(t))*p_rx_remaining(t). Paid starts=N_available*p_rx*paid_conversion, with delay. d and conditional hazards not identified by current sources.
architecture_recommendation.IR: Separate injectable-rescue incumbents, established Ekterly users, and newly treated entrants. Route preference informs injectable-to-oral opportunity; oral-to-oral choice needs incremental benefit and access evidence. Background prophylaxis is a separate consumption attribute, not a competing rescue-origin bucket.
architecture_recommendation.access: 80% conversion and1month delay remain assumptions. Pre-prescription access friction embedded in composite Rx probability; avoid another generic haircut. Historical filled-claim switching includes access and cannot be treated as Rx then discounted again without explicit mapping.
architecture_recommendation.taper: High-interest incumbent depletion and low-interest residual patients can create endogenous declining aggregate hazard. Physician reach and access can initially offset it. Do not impose a numeric decay from the first eight months; new-patient flow separate.

diagnostic_not_validation.meaning: About52.5% of historical any-switch incidence after conversion, with mismatched populations/endpoints. Shows10% is not automatically tiny; cannot establish actual destination share or best estimate.

model_action: No forecast coefficients or valuation changed. Current10% acquisition remains provisional; retire claims that it is empirically calibrated. Research bridge supplements canonical handoff.
stopping_rule: Existing evidence plus five targeted queries and selective primary full-text follow-up. No paid data, outreach, agents or fitting. No public joint dataset linking established Orladeyo control/satisfaction to subsequent PHVS choice identified. Do not replace unknown with average of incompatible studies.
